subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity needs & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-15T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity needs & next steps

Thanks for the time today, Daniel — great conversation. Quick recap so we have alignment before the technical follow-up.

Pain points you shared:
- Current inference latency spikes (P95 often > 350ms) on your current shared cluster, impacting real-time assistant workflows.
- Multi-tenant environments make you uncomfortable with model/data isolation requirements for PHI-sensitive flows.
- Cost unpredictability during peaks; need predictable unit economics for forecasting.

Goals we heard:
- Stable P95 latency < 150ms for the primary 2k token prompts.
- Sustained throughput target ~200 qps for peak windows, with short bursts to ~300 qps.
- Dedicated isolation (VPC + reserved GPUs) and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Recommended Dedicated plan (high level):
- Reserved capacity: 8x A100-class GPUs as the baseline, configured with pre-warmed KV cache and continuous batching.
- Burst/overflow: allow burst to 12 GPUs in your region (same hardware family) with cost controls.
- Autoscaling: policy to maintain P95 SLA while minimizing excess reserved slots; suggested cooldowns and queue thresholds to avoid noisy scaling.
- Isolation: customer-dedicated pool with private VPC peering and optional on-prem connector for sensitive workloads.
- SLA target: 99.9% availability for the dedicated pool, with per-route latency SLOs and automatic failover to a lower-cost model variant for graceful degradation.

Action items / next steps:
1) Technical deep dive with our SEs and infra team — propose Tue Apr 20 at 10:00am PT. (Please confirm.)
2) I'll share a capacity worksheet + rough estimate (attached) and a short SOW outline for reserved capacity billing.
3) Marissa to loop in procurement contacts and share SOC2 + compliance links.

Attachments: Aurora_Reqs_Dedicated_Capacity.pdf (requirements worksheet)

If anything above is off, flag and I’ll update. Otherwise we’ll use this as the basis for the tech session.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Hi Daniel — Rishi here (solutions). Quick responses inline to help prep the tech session: 

- Mapping qps to GPUs: for your workload shape (2k token average, mixed generate + chat) our rough estimate is 8x A100-80GB reserved to sustain ~200 qps with P95 <150ms when KV cache hit rates are high (~70%). If cache hit rates are lower we recommend additional capacity or a higher memory GPU family.
- Burst sizing: plan for burst to 12 GPUs; we throttle burst by configured seconds-of-burst and cost cap.
- Quantization: we support FP16 and int8 inference paths. For Aurora Health we’d run a short regen test to validate accuracy loss — most models maintain quality with dynamic quantization; we can bring bench numbers to the call.
- SOC2: yes — Redwood has SOC2 Type II; procurement can use this link: https://redwood.ai/compliance/soc2 (we'll attach the formal report under an NDA).

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (capacity & cost model) — contains the baseline sizing, burst model, and monthly cost estimates under different utilization scenarios.

Proposed tech session agenda (30–45 mins):
1) Run through production workload profile & current bottlenecks
2) Walk through dedicated pool architecture (VPC peering, KMS integration, audit logs)
3) Sizing + autoscaling policy options (baseline vs. burst)
4) Procurement & SOW timeline (docs needed, SOC2, lead times)

We still have Tue Apr 20 at 10:00am PT open; can confirm once Daniel locks it. I’ll bring a brief perf deck and the cost worksheet.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
